pages.text:
Conductance and electrochemical driving diﬀerence
Ij = gj(V − Ej).
A reversal potential makes one current zero, not necessarily the total current.
At V < E j, this outward-positive current is negative.

pages.title: Regenerative and terminating feedback
pages.text:
Regenerative and terminating feedback
Depolarization increases sodium activation, which can increase inward current.
Sodium availability then falls; potassium conductance rises; driving diﬀerences also change.
Current is conductance times driving diﬀerence.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 14 / 22

pages.title: An exact gate substep
pages.text:
An exact gate substep
Freeze V = V k during ∆t:
sk+1 = s∞(V k) + [sk − s∞(V k)]e−∆t/τs(V k).
This is a convex combination; no clipping is needed.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 19 / 22

pages.title: Accuracy of the coupled membrane calculation
pages.text:
Accuracy of the coupled membrane calculation
Exact substeps do not imply an exact coupled solution.
Check rest, gate bounds, rate limits, and common-time reﬁnement.
The sequential split is generally ﬁrst order in the full state; voltage alone may show higher
apparent order in a speciﬁc experiment.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 22 / 22
